SourceActivities: 21.1 What Went Wrong false parallel inference
21.2 Triangle Angle Sum by midpoint 180 rotations
21.3 Triangle Angle Sum by two translations

Task.Prompt: On paper draw an original nondegenerate Euclidean triangle and give TWO independent complete narrative proofs that interior angle measures sum 180 degrees: first via side-midpoint 180-degree rotations, second via two translations. Annotate images/parallel lines and diagnose Tyler's use of nonparallel lines.

Criteria.Criterion: identifies Tyler's unjustified nonparallel corresponding-angle step
writes a complete midpoint half-turn narrative proof of the sum
writes an independent two-translation angle-sum proof with labelled images
makes correct general Euclidean/parallel assumptions and coherent concluding narrative

Items.Prompt: Two triangles have identical orientation and displacement; are they translations?
Items.Expected: Yes if every corresponding point has the same directed displacement.

Items.Prompt: Parallelogram has adjacent interior angles 70 and ?
Items.Expected: 110 degrees, since parallel-line angles are supplementary.

Items.Prompt: Which alternate interior angle corresponds to a given line-pair angle?
Items.Expected: The opposite-side interior angle across the transversal when lines are parallel.

Items.Prompt: Which other triangle angles equal in two parallel horizontal lines cut by transversals?
Items.Expected: Corresponding/alternate angle pairs determined by matched rays, not the drawing alone.

Items.Prompt: Two approaches to parallel transversal angle equality?
Items.Expected: Translate for corresponding; half-turn about midpoint for alternate interior.

Items.Prompt: Half-turn about B maps D to A?
Items.Expected: Only if BD=BA. It always places the image on the opposite ray.

Items.Prompt: Why are intersection-line vertical angles equal?
Items.Expected: 180° rotation or equal supplementary linear pairs.

Items.Prompt: How verify collinearity of original and image points under a specified rigid move?
Items.Expected: Track the full line's image and its point membership.

Items.Prompt: How map congruent triangles ABC to A'B'C'?
Items.Expected: Translate a vertex, rotate about it to align a side, reflect if needed.

FirstPartyCooldown: EDULYTIKS_AUTHORED_COOLDOWN: triangle angles 43,57 and 80 degrees prove their 180 sum via parallel-line transformation, not scalar guessing
PaperHandoff: Teacher collects both labelled narrative proofs and critique, scores each 0/1/2 criterion, signs/dates feedback on paper under school policy. No runtime teacher grade asserted.

Cases.CORRECT: two independently valid general proofs and critique
Cases.EQUIVALENT: any nondegenerate triangle or rotated/transferred diagram giving same logical proof
Cases.WRONG: corresponding angles assumed equal when source lines nonparallel
Cases.INSUFFICIENT: three measured numbers sum 180 without general proof
Cases.MALFORMED: collinear triangle vertices or missing construction

StageD.Required: school/pathway exact lesson manual teacher scoring and persistence, authenticated E2E/tenant
